highlights: SCAP issued the 4 January purge directives removing militarists from public office and dissolving ultra-nationalistic societies, prompting a reorganization of the Shidehara Cabinet.
Emperor Hirohito promulgated the 1 January New Year Rescript reaffirming the Meiji Charter Oath and renouncing the doctrine of imperial divinity.
The Charter of the International Military Tribunal for the Far East was promulgated on 19 January to try major war criminals in Tokyo.
SCAP ordered the abolition of licensed prostitution on 21 January, nullifying all contracts binding women to involuntary servitude.
Allied authorities placed 394 Japanese aircraft factories, arsenals, and laboratories under custody as an initial step toward interim reparations.
General Orders No. 1 established the United States Army Military Government in Korea (USAMGIK), centralizing civil administration under non-tactical military government control.
Violent Korean demonstrations erupted across southern Korea opposing the Moscow Conference five-year trusteeship proposal, threatening general strikes until calmed by USAFIK leaders.

summary: Summation No. 4 documents non-military activities of the Allied occupation in Japan and southern Korea during January 1946, a pivotal month of institutional overhaul and democratic reform. In Japan, SCAP issued the sweeping 4 January purge directives banning militaristic organizations and disqualifying wartime leaders from public office, triggering a crisis and reorganization of the Shidehara Cabinet. Emperor Hirohito issued his historic New Year Rescript renouncing imperial divinity, while SCAP abolished licensed prostitution, promulgated the Charter for the International Military Tribunal for the Far East, and placed 394 industrial plants under custody for reparations. Severe economic strains persisted, marked by lagging food collections, runaway inflation, a ¥56 billion banknote issue, and critical coal and charcoal shortages, which catalyzed rapid labor unionization. In Korea, General Orders No. 1 formally integrated the United States Army Military Government in Korea (USAMGIK). Nationwide civil unrest erupted following the Moscow Conference trusteeship announcement, prompting US-Soviet talks in Seoul, while severe rice hoarding forced emergency economic controls. For historians, the report provides invaluable contemporary statistical data, organograms, and candid accounts of early demilitarization, institutional democratization, and the divergent political trajectories of occupied Japan and Korea.
